The '''1724 [[FLLA]] World Cup''' was the 14th edition of the [[FLLA World Cup]], the quadrennial international [[Arraby]] tournament contested by the senior men's national teams of the member associations of the [[FLLA]]. It was held in [[Areoix Lie]] across [[Acrola]] from 1 to 29 June 1724, and was won by [[Verusa]], who defeated [[Easuhura]] 3–1 in the final at the Zirohu National Stadium in [[Zirohu]] to claim their first FLLA World Cup title.

The 1724 edition was the first FLLA World Cup to be held in [[Acrola]] and the first to be contested by an expanded field of twenty-four teams. The expansion from sixteen to twenty-four finalists was approved by the FLLA Council in 1721, extending direct participation to a further eight associations and introducing a group stage of six groups feeding a sixteen-team knockout bracket. The format proved short-lived: the [[1728 FLLA World Cup|1728 edition]] reverted to a sixteen-team finals tournament, and the twenty-four-team field was not restored until the [[1732 FLLA World Cup|1732 edition]].

Played four years after the [[1720 FLLA World Cup|1720 tournament]] in [[Etirha]], the competition fell in the pre-rotation era of the FLLA World Cup, in which hosting rights were settled by an open vote of the FLLA Council rather than by a fixed confederation sequence. In keeping with the permanent-trophy tradition observed at every edition since the [[1700 FLLA World Cup|1700 tournament]], the host association commissioned a bespoke permanent trophy, '''The Akwene''', which was presented to the champions alongside the rotating [[FLLA World Cup#The Andah Cup|Andah Cup]], the silver-and-gold sculpture in continuous use since the [[1716 FLLA World Cup|1716 edition]]. The host nation [[Areoix Lie]] reached the semi-finals in the competition's first staging on Acrolan soil, the deepest run by an [[ACFVL]] side at the FLLA World Cup to that date, before finishing fourth.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/1724/tournament-summary|title=Summary report of the 1724 FLLA World Cup|publisher=[[FLLA]]|date=12 August 1724}}</ref>

==Host selection==

The 1724 FLLA World Cup was awarded under the informal pre-rotation framework that governed the competition between the [[1700 FLLA World Cup|1700 edition]] and the adoption of the confederation rotation policy in 1740. Under the practice then in force, the FLLA Council retained an open invitation for candidate associations from all seven confederations to lodge expressions of interest, with the final decision taken by simple majority vote of the Council following a technical assessment by the FLLA Secretariat.

Three associations lodged formal bids ahead of the deadline of 30 June 1721: [[Areoix Lie]] (representing the [[ACFVL]]), [[Quidic]] (representing the [[QUFVL]]) and [[Taval]] (representing the [[MSFVL]]). The bid submitted by the Areoix Lie Arraby Federation, the first ever lodged by an [[Acrola|Acrolan]] association, prevailed at the FLLA Council meeting of 14 October 1721 by fifteen votes to nine. The decision made [[Areoix Lie]] the first Acrolan nation to stage the competition and was widely framed in the [[ACFVL]] as the confederation's coming of age within the worldwide game, four editions after [[Areoix Lie]] had first entered the old Ayuma Cup as one of its earliest non-Ayuman participants.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/news/1721/areoix-lie-confirmed|title=Areoix Lie confirmed as 1724 FLLA World Cup hosts|publisher=[[FLLA]]|date=14 October 1721}}</ref>

The Areoix Lie bid was supported in the FLLA Secretariat's technical assessment by the federal government's pledge of {{lahn}}120&nbsp;million towards stadium construction and harbour and rail improvements across the six proposed host cities, and by the strategic case for staging the first FLLA World Cup in [[Acrola]] in advance of the planned expansion of the finals. The decision passed amid lobbying by the [[AYFVL]] secretariat in favour of a return to [[Ayuma]], an objection the FLLA Council noted but did not sustain.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/news/1721/bid-assessment|title=Technical assessment of the 1724 FLLA World Cup candidate bids|publisher=[[FLLA]]|date=22 September 1721}}</ref>

==Participating teams and officials==

===Qualification===

The 1724 qualification programme was the first conducted to the twenty-four-team finals format. Places at the finals were allocated across the seven [[FLLA]] confederations by the FLLA Council in November 1721, with the host association qualifying automatically as of right. The allocation distributed six places to the [[AYFVL]], four to the [[ACFVL]] (including the host), three each to the [[ATFVL]], [[MSFVL]], [[QUFVL]] and [[MAFVL]], and two to the [[NAFVL]]. Each confederation administered its own qualifying competition; the qualified teams are listed below.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/1721/berth-allocation-1724|title=Continental berth allocation for the 1724 FLLA World Cup|publisher=[[FLLA]]|date=18 November 1721}}</ref>

The qualifying programme produced two outcomes of note. The first was the qualification of the defending [[1720 FLLA World Cup|1720]] runners-up [[Lycroa]], who reached the 1724 finals as one of the six [[AYFVL]] qualifiers fourteen years before the [[Lycroan reunification]]; the side competed as a confederation of the pre-union Lycroan polities under the single Lycroan banner then recognised by the FLLA. The second was the qualification of three [[ACFVL]] sides alongside the host, the largest [[Acrola|Acrolan]] representation at any FLLA World Cup to that point, reflecting the confederation's investment in the game ahead of its first hosting.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.acfvl.org/1723/qualification-summary|title=ACFVL 1724 FLLA World Cup qualification summary|publisher=[[ACFVL]]|date=4 December 1723}}</ref>

===Final draw===

The final draw for the group stage was held at the Zirohu Civic Hall in [[Zirohu]] on 20 January 1724. The twenty-four qualified teams were drawn into six groups of four on the basis of their pre-tournament [[FLLA]] standings, with the host [[Areoix Lie]] and the five highest-ranked sides placed in the seeded pot and allocated to the six group positions.

===Officials===

The FLLA Referees Committee appointed thirteen refereeing trios drawn from a pool of eleven nations. The opening match between the hosts [[Areoix Lie]] and [[Etirha]] was refereed by Malvio Renza of [[Verusa]] ([[AYFVL]]); the final was officiated by Hanu Tepaia of [[Sattle]] ([[ACFVL]]), the first Acrolan referee appointed to an FLLA World Cup final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/1724/officials-announced|title=Match officials confirmed for the 1724 FLLA World Cup|publisher=[[FLLA]]|date=8 May 1724}}</ref>

==Squads==

Each participating squad consisted of 18 players, at least two of whom were required to be goalkeepers, under the squad regulation then in force; the allocation was increased to 20 players at the [[1736 FLLA World Cup|1736 edition]] and to the present 22 at the [[1740 FLLA World Cup|1740 edition]]. A total of 432 players were registered for the tournament. Each participating national association was required to confirm its final squad with the FLLA no later than seven days before the opening match.

==Venues==

Six stadiums in six host cities were used in the final tournament, all located in [[Areoix Lie]]. Two of the six, the Zirohu National Stadium and the Vurahi Harbour Ground, were newly built for the tournament; the remaining four were existing Areoix Lie venues that received targeted upgrades to seating under the host federation's preparation programme. The opening match and the final were both held at the Zirohu National Stadium in the host's largest city of [[Zirohu]]; the two semi-finals were divided between the Vurahi Harbour Ground in [[Vurahi]] and the Nakahiki Federal Stadium in [[Nakahiki]].

===Venue profiles===

The '''Zirohu National Stadium''', in the host's largest city of [[Zirohu]], was the principal venue of the tournament and the largest stadium on the [[Acrola|Acrolan]] continent at the time of its completion in April 1724. The 70,000-seat ground hosted the opening match on 1 June between the hosts [[Areoix Lie]] and [[Etirha]], one quarter-final, two round-of-sixteen ties, six group-stage fixtures and the [[#Final|final]] on 29 June, which drew an attendance of 68,200, the highest single-match crowd of the tournament.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aaf.acr/venues/zirohu-national-stadium|title=Zirohu National Stadium: design and inauguration|publisher=Areoix Lie Arraby Federation|date=4 April 1724}}</ref>

The '''Vurahi Harbour Ground''' in [[Vurahi]], a 58,000-seat venue built for the tournament on a reclaimed harbour site, hosted the first of the two [[#Semi-finals|semi-finals]] between [[Verusa]] and the hosts [[Areoix Lie]], one quarter-final, one round-of-sixteen tie and six group-stage fixtures. The '''Nakahiki Federal Stadium''' in [[Nakahiki]], a 50,000-seat ground, hosted the second [[#Semi-finals|semi-final]] between [[Easuhura]] and [[Lycroa]], the [[#Third place playoff|third-place playoff]] and six group-stage fixtures. The remaining three venues, the Xalavi Civic Stadium in [[Xalavi]], the Mahana Coastal Ground in [[Mahana]] and the Nikahatu Sports Ground in [[Nikahatu]], each staged knockout and group-stage fixtures as set out above.

==Format==

The twenty-four qualified teams were divided into six groups of four for the group stage, drawn at the [[#Final draw|final draw]] on 20 January 1724. Each group operated on a single round-robin basis, with each team playing three matches; teams were awarded three points for a win, one for a draw and none for a defeat. The six group winners, the six group runners-up and the four best third-placed teams advanced to a sixteen-team knockout stage, while the remaining eight were eliminated. Tiebreakers between teams level on points were applied in the following order: overall goal difference, overall goals scored, head-to-head record, and, if necessary, a drawing of lots by the FLLA Organising Committee.

In the knockout stage, fixtures were single-elimination ties played over 90 minutes; ties level at the end of normal time were extended by a single 30-minute period of [[wikipedia:Extra time|extra time]], with a [[wikipedia:Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shoot-out]] used to decide ties that remained level after extra time. The two semi-final losers contested a [[#Third place playoff|third-place playoff]] on 28 June, the day before the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/1723/regulations-1724|title=Regulations of the 1724 FLLA World Cup: group-stage and knockout format|publisher=[[FLLA]]|date=20 November 1723}}</ref>

==Group stage==

The twenty-four qualified teams were drawn into six groups of four. Each group operated on a single round-robin basis, with each team playing three matches; the top two finishers in each group advanced to the [[#Knockout stage|knockout stage]] along with the four best third-placed teams across the six groups, while the remaining sides were eliminated. Group rankings were settled first on points, then on goal difference and goals scored.

All times listed are Standard Areoix Time (AOT, UTC+11).

==Knockout stage==

The knockout stage involved the sixteen teams that advanced from the group stage. Matches still level after 90 minutes were extended by a 30-minute period of [[wikipedia:Extra time|extra time]]; if scores remained tied after extra time, the tie was decided by [[wikipedia:Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shoot-out]]. Two of the sixteen knockout-stage ties were decided after extra time, one of them by penalty shoot-out. The most widely noted result of the round of sixteen was the elimination of the [[ATFVL]] qualifying winners [[Raledria]] by the hosts [[Areoix Lie]] in the quarter-finals, the first time an [[Acrola|Acrolan]] side had reached the last four of the competition.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/1724/knockout-summary|title=Statistical summary of the 1724 FLLA World Cup knockout stage|publisher=[[FLLA]]|date=2 July 1724}}</ref>

===Round of 16===

The six group winners and six runners-up were joined by the four best third-placed teams. The host nation [[Areoix Lie]] opened the knockout stage with a 3–1 win over the [[MSFVL]] third-placed qualifier [[Taval]] at the Vurahi Harbour Ground, while the eventual champions [[Verusa]] and runners-up [[Easuhura]] advanced with comfortable wins over [[Trian]] and [[Etirha]] respectively. The only tie of the round to require extra time was the goalless meeting of [[Praesyu]] and [[United Delet]], which [[Praesyu]] won 4–2 on penalties at the Nakahiki Federal Stadium.

===Quarter-finals===

The four quarter-finals sent the hosts [[Areoix Lie]] into the semi-finals for the first time in the country's history. [[Areoix Lie]] beat the [[ATFVL]] qualifying winners [[Raledria]] 1–0 at the Vurahi Harbour Ground through a second-half goal by forward Tane Maraki, a result celebrated across the host nation as the high point of the tournament. [[Verusa]] beat [[Emara]] 2–1 at the Zirohu National Stadium, [[Easuhura]] beat [[Dahe]] 2–0 at the Xalavi Civic Stadium, and [[Lycroa]] beat [[Praesyu]] 2–1 after extra time at the Mahana Coastal Ground.

===Semi-finals===

The first semi-final at the Vurahi Harbour Ground was contested between [[Verusa]] and the hosts [[Areoix Lie]], the latter making the first FLLA World Cup semi-final appearance by an [[ACFVL]] side. [[Areoix Lie]] took the lead through forward Tane Maraki in the 34th minute before [[Verusa]] recovered to win 2–1, the equaliser scored by forward Toren Vasque and the winner by captain Adren Caldori twelve minutes from time. The result ended the host nation's run and took [[Verusa]] to their first FLLA World Cup final.

The second semi-final at the Nakahiki Federal Stadium was decided by a single first-half goal from [[Easuhura]] forward Veno Halmeri, who turned in a low cross in the 21st minute to settle a cautious meeting with [[Lycroa]]. The result took [[Easuhura]] to their first FLLA World Cup final and eliminated [[Lycroa]] at the semi-final stage for the second consecutive edition.

===Third place playoff===

The third-place playoff was contested between the two losing semi-finalists at the Nakahiki Federal Stadium on 28 June, the day before the [[#Final|final]]. [[Lycroa]] beat the hosts [[Areoix Lie]] 2–1 to take third place, recovering from an early deficit through second-half goals by forwards Mario Calveni and Loris Maresto. The result gave [[Lycroa]] third place, four years after their runners-up finish at the [[1720 FLLA World Cup|1720 edition]], and left the hosts [[Areoix Lie]] in fourth, a placing that nonetheless stood as the deepest run by an [[ACFVL]] side at the competition for several editions.

===Final===
{{Main|1724 FLLA World Cup final}}

The final was contested between [[Verusa]] and [[Easuhura]] on 29 June 1724 at the Zirohu National Stadium in [[Zirohu]] in front of an attendance of 68,200, the highest crowd of the tournament. The match was the first FLLA World Cup final to be contested between two [[AYFVL]] sides since the [[1712 FLLA World Cup|1712 edition]], and was played in front of a live radio audience across [[Areoix Lie]] and relayed to several [[Acrola|Acrolan]] partner stations.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/1724/final-report|title=Match report: 1724 FLLA World Cup final, Verusa 3–1 Easuhura|publisher=[[FLLA]]|date=30 June 1724}}</ref>

[[Verusa]] took the lead in the 14th minute through forward Toren Vasque, who finished a low cross from the right to score his sixth goal of the tournament. [[Easuhura]] equalised seven minutes before half time through forward Veno Halmeri, but [[Verusa]] regained the lead early in the second half through captain Adren Caldori and added a third in the 74th minute through forward Joran Renvis to seal a 3–1 victory and the country's first FLLA World Cup title. The win was secured by a [[Verusa|Verusan]] side that had conceded only four goals across its seven matches behind goalkeeper Joren Olant, who was named the tournament's [[#Awards|outstanding goalkeeper]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.vrt.ver/sport/1724/final|title=Verusa win first world title in Zirohu|publisher=Verusan Radio Service|date=29 June 1724}}</ref>

==Statistics==

===Goalscoring===

A total of 125 goals were scored across the 52 matches of the tournament, an average of 2.40 per match. [[Verusa]] finished as the leading goalscoring nation with 15 goals across their seven matches, ahead of [[Easuhura]] and [[Lycroa]] (each 12) and the hosts [[Areoix Lie]] (11). The table below lists the leading goalscoring nations of the tournament.

The leading individual goalscorer at the tournament was [[Verusa|Verusan]] forward Toren Vasque with six goals across [[Verusa]]'s seven matches, a tally that earned him the [[#Awards|FLLA Marskval]] as the competition's top scorer. The next most prolific scorer was [[Easuhura|Easuhuran]] forward Veno Halmeri with five goals, including the opening goal of the [[#Semi-finals|semi-final]] against [[Lycroa]] and the [[Easuhura|Easuhuran]] consolation in the [[#Final|final]]; the host nation's Tane Maraki of [[Areoix Lie]] finished with four goals across the knockout stage.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/1724/individual-goalscoring|title=Individual goalscoring at the 1724 FLLA World Cup|publisher=[[FLLA]]|date=4 July 1724}}</ref>

===Discipline===

The FLLA Disciplinary Committee issued a total of 121 yellow cards and 5 red cards across the 52 matches of the tournament, an average of 2.33 yellows and 0.10 reds per match. Two of the five dismissals occurred in the knockout stage.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/discipline/1724-summary|title=FLLA Disciplinary Committee: 1724 FLLA World Cup disciplinary summary|publisher=[[FLLA]]|date=8 July 1724}}</ref>

==Awards==

Three individual awards and one team recognition were presented at the close of the 1724 FLLA World Cup. The '''FLLA Vairan Ball''' for the most outstanding player of the tournament was awarded to the [[Verusa|Verusan]] captain and midfielder Adren Caldori, whose goals in the [[#Semi-finals|semi-final]] and [[#Final|final]] settled both of [[Verusa]]'s closing matches. The '''FLLA Marskval''' for the top scorer was awarded to [[Verusa|Verusan]] forward Toren Vasque with six goals, and the '''FLLA Bastion''' for the best goalkeeper to [[Verusa|Verusan]] goalkeeper Joren Olant, who conceded four goals across [[Verusa]]'s seven matches. The '''FLLA Best Young Player Award''' was awarded to the 19-year-old [[Areoix Lie]] forward Tane Maraki, whose four knockout-stage goals carried the hosts to the semi-finals.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/1724/awards-record|title=Awards record of the 1724 FLLA World Cup|publisher=[[FLLA]]|date=30 June 1724}}</ref>

==Trophies==

In keeping with the permanent-trophy tradition observed at every FLLA World Cup since the [[1700 FLLA World Cup|1700 edition]], the host association commissioned a bespoke permanent trophy for the 1724 tournament. '''The Akwene''', a sculpted figure cast by an Areoix Lie atelier and commissioned by the Areoix Lie Arraby Federation, was presented to the winners alongside the rotating [[FLLA World Cup#The Andah Cup|Andah Cup]] at the closing ceremony at the Zirohu National Stadium. Following the [[#Final|3–1 win]] by [[Verusa]] over [[Easuhura]], The Akwene was transferred to permanent retention by the [[Verusa|Verusan]] association and is displayed at the Verusan National Museum, while the rotating Andah Cup, the silver-and-gold sculpture in continuous use since the [[1716 FLLA World Cup|1716 edition]], was held by [[Verusa]] for the year following the tournament before its return to the FLLA ahead of the [[1728 FLLA World Cup|1728 edition]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/1724/permanent-trophy|title=The Akwene: 1724 FLLA World Cup permanent trophy|publisher=[[FLLA]]|date=29 June 1724}}</ref>

==Aftermath==

[[Verusa]]'s victory was the country's first FLLA World Cup title and the first secured by an [[AYFVL]] side since the [[1716 FLLA World Cup|1716 edition]], won by [[Raledria]] in [[Easuhura]]. The result was widely celebrated across [[Verusa]], where the team returned to a civic reception in the capital and the permanent trophy [[#Trophies|The Akwene]] was placed on display at the Verusan National Museum, where it has remained since.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.vrt.ver/news/1724/homecoming|title=Verusa celebrate first world title|publisher=Verusan Radio Service|date=2 July 1724}}</ref>

The tournament was judged an organisational success for the [[ACFVL]] and for the host nation, whose run to the semi-finals was the deepest by an [[Acrola|Acrolan]] side at the competition for several editions. The twenty-four-team format introduced in 1724 proved short-lived, however: citing the cost and scheduling burden of the larger finals on prospective hosts, the FLLA Council voted in 1725 to revert to a sixteen-team tournament for the [[1728 FLLA World Cup|1728 edition]] in [[Ayuma]], won by [[Emara]]. The twenty-four-team field was not restored until the [[1732 FLLA World Cup|1732 edition]], and the present thirty-two-team format was adopted at the [[1740 FLLA World Cup|1740 edition]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/1725/format-review|title=FLLA Council reverts to sixteen-team finals for 1728|publisher=[[FLLA]]|date=18 October 1725}}</ref>

The edition fell in the pre-rotation era of the competition and fourteen years before the [[Lycroan reunification]] of September 1738; [[Lycroa]]'s third-place finish, achieved by a side drawn from the pre-union Lycroan polities, is recorded in later [[Lycroa|Lycroan]] football histories as the strongest showing of the pre-reunification national team.
